scope: Private ingestion-owner committed readback with native alarm storage and the production User coordinator alarm handler; synthetic D1/R2 and no-op child Workflows. The fixture supplies the production alarm scheduler to readback after the existing owner fixture committed the intent; it does not exercise a public upload route or the complete hosted Turn service. Four phase-matched pairs, ABBA order, two synthetic User identities with valid seven-day Trial records, candidate reset on two of four pairs after a test-only three-second future alarm and confirmed storage.sync; that delay remains included in measured candidate time. Control waits for a real next-five-minute cadence represented by a native Workflow timer calling the current global dispatcher; this is not a measurement of the Cron Trigger transport. No production Cron transport latency, extraction completion, production authenticated API latency or CPU comparison is claimed.
notes: Four pairs share one discovery phase and two synthetic Trial Users; this is not a multi-region or p95 distribution.
Control uses a native Workflow timer to reproduce the next five-minute discovery cadence and the current global dispatcher; actual Cron Trigger transport is excluded.

The fixture commits with the existing owner adapter, then runs held-owner committed readback with its supplied native alarm scheduler. The actual User coordinator alarm handler dispatches the identity. It does not invoke the complete hosted Turn entry service.
Two candidate cases use a test-only 3000 ms future alarm, await storage.sync and force ctx.abort; the full artificial delay is included in measurements.
Actor reset during immediate handoff had an earlier unlocalized deadline failure; retained separately, without a crash-latency guarantee.
Child Workflows are no-op probes; candidate fixtures are marked failed afterward through the actual failure owner solely to release fixture admission. Real extraction completion is not measured.
